01 · CLIENT

The journey begins in a browser.

Orxan in Baku enters booking.com and searches for a hotel in Gabala. Static assets may come from a nearby CDN edge; dynamic availability needs backend services.

🔒 https://www.booking.com

02 · GLOBAL ROUTING

A healthy region is selected.

DNS/global load balancing considers latency and health. A region is a geographic cloud location; each region can contain one or more independent Kubernetes clusters.

Request → EU West, the closest healthy region.

EU West
Cluster A
EU Central
Cluster B
Asia
Cluster C
03 · CLUSTER

The cluster supplies infrastructure.

A cluster is control plane plus worker nodes. Nodes contribute CPU, RAM, network and storage. Kubernetes places Pods on those nodes and continuously reconciles desired state with reality.

Control plane · API · Scheduler · Controllers

04 · AVAILABILITY

Search checks cache, then data.

The Kubernetes Service routes to a ready Hotels/Search Pod. Redis answers hot availability quickly. On a miss, the service reads the source-of-truth database and refreshes the cache.

05 · RESULT

Availability is returned.

The frontend receives available rooms, price and a short-lived offer identifier. Cache improves speed, but the booking flow must validate availability again before confirmation.

06 · BOOKING & PAYMENT

Slow work becomes reliable events.

Booking validates inventory; Payment calls an external provider with an idempotency key. Kafka or RabbitMQ can feed workers. If the response is unknown, reconciliation checks provider state—never blindly charges again.
